A public article about careful reading

Fixture Writer

Start with the original source

A careful reader begins by identifying the author and the specific document being read. The surrounding discussion can provide context, but a reply is a different source and should never silently become part of the original article.

Keeping a picture beside the paragraph that explains it matters. Saving only a link to a picture makes an offline copy much less useful, while replacing the source with a summary loses the details a reader might want to inspect closely.

  • Keep the author's paragraph order.
  • Retain useful images and captions.

The final paragraph belongs to this article too. A successful import reaches this ending, preserves the distinction between a still image and a video preview, and leaves the original source available for anything the local reader cannot reproduce.
